correctness.rationale: The four-state labeled de Bruijn path relation proves in both directions that a periodic output has an antecedent with period dividing k times its output period precisely when a Boolean matrix for its word has a closed walk of length k. Any cyclic four-vertex directed graph has a simple cycle of length at most four. Exhaustive closure of the two Boolean generators for all 256 rules, with all relations compared under packed-bit and independent row-tuple representations and girths rechecked by graph DFS, proves the exact 156/82/16/2 strata, exceptional rule lists, and universal sharp witness length three. The 256-row CSV and 65,024 finite-ring comparisons provide reproducible corroboration, not substitutes for the closure argument.

value.rationale: Period preservation of factor maps is central to the weak periodic point condition and to obstructions for constructing sections. This complete family-wide optimal lifting-index classification sharpens the qualitative yes/no criterion into four genuinely distinct arithmetic regimes, pinpoints the only two fourfold extremizers and proves a uniform optimal three-symbol witness threshold. The object and invariant are canonical, not an ad hoc slice; the exact cutoff and extremal rigidity give substantive structural information beyond individual known examples.
